title: Integrated Response: IPM, Biosecurity, CAPA & Recovery

content.overview: The case response should connect the best-supported mechanism to proportionate controls, authority boundaries, recovery metrics and an effectiveness check. The plan should still work if residual uncertainty remains.

vocabulary.definition: The specific risk or failure mode an intervention is intended to reduce.
Risk that remains after current controls are applied.
Predefined evidence used to judge whether the intervention or CAPA achieved the intended control objective.

sections.title: Match controls to the mechanism
sections.body: A propagation-linked pathogen risk, media-associated pest, irrigation failure and resistance concern require different control packages. Select controls because they address the evidence-supported pathway.

sections.title: Integrate tactics without creating new failure modes
sections.body: Check beneficial-organism compatibility, environmental effects, sanitation interactions and resistance selection pressure when combining controls.

sections.title: Build recovery and CAPA into the plan
sections.body: Define who owns each action, what recovery measurement will be used, when it will be checked and what result triggers escalation, reopening or closure.

workedExamples: If the case points to a contaminated propagation workflow, a strong plan may combine hold/movement controls, workflow correction, tool/process validation and targeted retesting rather than relying on one treatment step.
commonMistakes: Choosing controls before the failure mechanism is defined.
Closing when the action is performed rather than when effectiveness is demonstrated.
content.practicalApplication: Write a case response plan with immediate containment, targeted control, owner, authorization, compatibility check, recovery metric, effectiveness window and residual risk.
content.summary: Integrated response turns diagnosis into a controlled learning loop rather than a one-time treatment decision.
